title: The owner's inputs: contracts, reviewers, tasks, model access (prepared)
request: Turn the owner's answers into files: the prediction contracts for HyperAck and churn as solution files checked by studio.solution, the reviewers' names, two or three real tasks with a success criterion and a time budget, and the provider check. Nothing is guessed: an unanswered question stays visibly open. The owner said to do everything that does not depend on other people, so the part that needs the owner was prepared, not filled in.
spec: evaluation/contracts/*.json (target, prediction moment, forbidden columns with reasons, time and group columns, metric) each loading as a valid Solution; reviewers, tasks and the provider check recorded; every unanswered question left open.
plan: Write evaluation/OWNER_ANSWERS.md with one block per question, listing the data's own column names so the answers can use them.
Write dclab_rnd/agent_eval/owner_inputs.py: status lists what is open and checks each contract loads as a Solution that names only columns its data has.
Record the provider check from 14.2's live runs and mark it for the owner to confirm; leave the contracts unwritten.
Review with the other Part 3 kits; fix the findings; commit.

decisions.decision: The contracts are not written by the assistant.
decisions.why: The prediction moment decides which columns leak; it is the owner's knowledge of the business, and a guessed contract would make every later score look valid while resting on a guess.

decisions.decision: An answer the assistant recorded is listed as unconfirmed.
decisions.why: The provider check came from the live runs, not from the owner; status must not count it as the owner's answer.

change: New evaluation/OWNER_ANSWERS.md (one block per question with the files' columns), dclab_rnd/agent_eval/owner_inputs.py (status and the contract check), tests/test_owner_inputs.py.

findings.defect: A contract counted as ready without being valid.
findings.scenario: Ready for HyperAck was true when no HyperAck question was open and any hyperack*.json file existed, even if the check marked that file invalid; the text 'can be re-run under its contract' implied a re-run nothing performs. The provider check, pre-filled by the author, counted as answered.
findings.fix: Readiness requires a valid contract and is worded 'contract loads'; an answer the assistant recorded is listed as unconfirmed.
findings.impact: The status would have told the owner that the HyperAck contract was ready while the file failed its own check, so a re-run of the research under that contract, which nothing performs, could have been believed done; and a provider check the assistant had filled in counted as the owner's answer.
findings.open: Ten of the eleven questions still wait for the owner, and the two contracts are not written.

outcome: Prepared (c291a1b), open on the owner's answers: 10 of 11 questions open; the provider check recorded from 14.2 and marked for the owner to confirm; the two contracts not written.
lessons: When a decision belongs to the owner, build the form and the check, and leave the answer open; never fill it in to make a package look done.
risks: Filling a contract or an answer on the owner's behalf turns a guess into a recorded fact; every unanswered question must stay visibly open.
A readiness flag that checks only that a file exists will report a broken contract as ready.
An answer the assistant wrote down (such as the provider check) must be marked unconfirmed until the owner confirms it.
Status wording must not imply work nothing performs, such as a re-run under the contract.
